meta: Dozens of messages pile up, and customers wait too long and leave. How AI helps: ready-made replies, drafts for angry customers, chatbots for simple questions, and real policies only.

muc.title: Messages piling up
muc.text: After the livestream, dozens of customer messages pour in. Mark can't keep up, and customers wait too long and leave.

muc.title: A set of ready-made replies
muc.text: Bit suggests: ask AI to write ready-made replies for common questions, like price, size, shipping fees and returns, then save them as quick replies.

muc.title: Hard messages: let AI draft
muc.text: When a customer is upset, paste the message into AI and ask for a polite draft with an apology and a concrete fix. Edit it before you send.

muc.title: Automatic chatbot replies
muc.text: If you use a chatbot to reply automatically, let it answer only simple questions, and pass anything about money, returns or complaints to a real person.

muc.title: Don't promise what the shop doesn't do
muc.text: Careful: AI may promise things the shop doesn't offer, like 60-day returns. Always put your real policy in the prompt and check before sending.

muc.title: Five ready-made replies
muc.text: List the five questions customers asked most this week, ask AI for friendly sample answers, edit them and save them as quick replies.
